research_text:
## Research brief

### API and meaning of the finding

`java.security.KeyPair` is a holder for a public key and a private key. Its constructor stores references to the supplied keys; `getPublic()` and `getPrivate()` return the respective references. Oracle says the class enforces no security and that an initialized pair should be treated like a private key. Source: `https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/security/KeyPair.html`. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/security/KeyPair.html))

The reported finding concerns the **analyzer’s observation of a `KeyPair` object’s event sequence and provenance**, not a Java runtime exception or a particular key value. The rule specifies a constructor event followed by zero or more accessor events, and separately requires a `generatedKeypair` predicate if the constructor event was not observed. The supplied finding does not include the trace, call site, analyzer configuration, or predicate-propagation results needed to determine why it was reported. Source: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/KeyPair.crysl`. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/KeyPair.crysl))

### Documented usage and remediation

- Oracle documents direct construction from `PublicKey` and `PrivateKey` references and access through the two getters. It does **not** prescribe a CrySL event sequence or a specific remediation for this detector finding. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/security/KeyPair.html))
- Oracle documents `KeyPairGenerator` as a way to generate a public/private pair. It recommends explicitly initializing the generator rather than relying on provider defaults, which can vary and change. That is general API guidance, **not a finding-specific fix**. Source: `https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/security/KeyPairGenerator.html`. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/security/KeyPairGenerator.html))
- The CrySL predicates are analysis requirements, not security checks performed by `KeyPair`. The rule does not specify a check that the two components mathematically correspond. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/KeyPair.crysl))

### Compatibility and migration

- **Java serialization:** Java SE 25 documents `KeyPair` as serializable, with `publicKey` and `privateKey` fields and serial version UID `-7565189502268009837L`. This alone does not establish compatibility for a particular provider’s key objects or for a changed application format. Source: `https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/serialized-form.html#java.security.KeyPair`. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/serialized-form.html))
- **Individual key encodings:** Oracle documents X.509 `SubjectPublicKeyInfo` and PKCS #8 as example external key formats. `Key.getEncoded()` and `getFormat()` can return `null` when encoding is unsupported. Serialized keys may contain sensitive information. Source: `https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/security/Key.html`. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/security/Key.html))
- **Pair PEM encoding:** Java SE 25’s *preview* `PEMEncoder` documents encoding a `KeyPair` as a PKCS #8 v2.0 `OneAsymmetricKey` structure with PEM type `PRIVATE KEY`; its preview decoder documents returning a `KeyPair` when the encoding also contains a public key. Preview features require enablement and may change or be removed. Sources: `https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/security/PEMEncoder.html` and `https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/security/PEMDecoder.html`. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/security/PEMEncoder.html?utm_source=openai))
- **Version and migration limits:** `KeyPair` is documented since Java 1.1; the cited PEM APIs are since Java 25 and preview in that release. The cited sources do not provide a migration path specifically for this finding, nor do they establish that changing how a pair is obtained preserves existing keys, persisted data, or wire compatibility. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/security/KeyPair.html))

### Exact rule in the supplied CrySL source

The source’s matching and ordering clauses are, verbatim: ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/KeyPair.crysl))

```text
SPEC java.security.KeyPair
```

```text
EVENTS
	c1: KeyPair(publicKey, privateKey);
	Con := c1;

	gpu1: retPublicKey = getPublic();
	GetPubl := gpu1;

	gpr1: retPrivateKey = getPrivate();
	GetPriv := gpr1;

ORDER
	Con, (GetPubl | GetPriv)*
```

The source declares the constructor variables as `java.security.PublicKey` and `java.security.PrivateKey`. Thus the listed constructor event has **two typed arguments**, while the listed accessor events have **empty parameter lists**. The specified class is `java.security.KeyPair`; the rule does not state a name-only match for methods on arbitrary receiver types. **A method merely sharing `getPublic` or `getPrivate` on an unrelated type is not what this rule specifies.** The file does not itself document an analyzer implementation’s resolution behavior. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/KeyPair.crysl))

The exact requirements are: ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/KeyPair.crysl))

```text
REQUIRES
	generatedPrivkey[privateKey];
	generatedPubkey[publicKey];
	noCallTo[Con] => generatedKeypair[this, _];
```

The rule also declares `generatedKeypair` after `Con` and the corresponding generated-key predicates after each accessor. The cited URL points to the mutable `master` branch; its contents were inspected, but the supplied SHA-256 and the revision used for the finding were not independently verified. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/KeyPair.crysl))
